so maybe we'll move on to investigating this characteristic polynomial a little bit further. But to do this, first of all, I like to recall the trace. So the trace of the matrix, which you should have seen in linear algebra 1, is just the sum of all the diagonal elements. and a quick lever is that if we take two n by n matrices a and b we have that the trace of a b is equal to the trace of b a for all matrices a and b. So the proof of this is simple. So the The trace of AB is just the sum over i of the ii -th entry of the matrix IB, AB. But we can write down that explicitly. That's just the sum over j of aij bji. But these are finite sums, so we can just swap the i -sum and the j -sum around. So this is the sum over j, sum over i of b, j, i, a, i, j, and we see that then this is Precisely the same expansion of the trace of the matrix B, A.
